options: A single command that creates all of a project's branches automatically
A team-wide agreement about what branches exist, what each represents, and the rules for moving code between them
A rule that forbids ever deleting a branch
A Salesforce-specific feature with no general Git equivalent
questions.explain: A branching strategy is a deliberate, agreed-upon convention — not something each developer improvises individually — about what branches mean and how code flows between them.

questions.q: In Git Flow, which branch type is created directly from main to address an urgent production issue, without waiting for the next scheduled release?
options: feature/*
release/*
hotfix/*
develop
questions.explain: hotfix/* branches are cut directly from main specifically for urgent fixes that can't wait for the normal develop → release → main cycle.

questions.q: In environment branching, what does merging a change from the qa branch into the uat branch typically represent?
options: Deleting the QA sandbox
Promoting a change to the next environment in the pipeline — literally merging the branch representing the current org into the branch representing the next one
Reverting a production hotfix
Creating a brand-new scratch org
questions.explain: Under environment branching, each long-lived branch maps one-to-one to a specific org, so promoting a change up the pipeline is literally merging forward through that chain of branches.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should actually determine which branching strategy a Salesforce team picks?
options: Whichever strategy is most popular on blogs
The team's actual release cadence and process — frequent small releases favor simpler models, scheduled release trains with approval gates favor more structure
The number of developers on the team, with no other factor relevant
Whichever strategy requires the fewest branch names
questions.explain: The lesson argues there's no universally "best" strategy — the right choice depends on how the team actually ships, matching the branching model's structure to the team's real release cadence and approval process.

questions.q: What does the develop branch represent in Git Flow?
options: What's currently live in production
The integration branch where finished features accumulate before a release
A single developer's personal scratch space
An archived, read-only copy of old releases
questions.explain: develop is the integration branch in Git Flow — features merge into it as they're finished, and a release/* branch is later cut from develop when enough features are ready to stabilize for release.
